newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan yen-denominated exports lowest in 7 years.
newsitem.headline: Japan yen-denominated exports lowest in 7 years.

text.p: Japan's ratio of yen-denominated export trade was at its lowest level in seven years at the end of September 1996, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.
Yen-denominated foreign exchange settlements in connection with exports fell to 35.2 percent in September from 35.9 percent at end-March 1996, the lowest since 1989, according an MITI report.
This was due partly to the desire by trading firms, and especially their overseas subsidiaries, to avoid currency risks, a MITI official said.
Yen-denominated export settlements hit a peak of 42.8 percent at the end of March 1993.

"When you consider the yen's recent depreciation, it actually makes a lot more sense for these companies, and their foreign subsidiaries in particular, to denominate more of their trade in dollars or other currencies," he said.
Yen-denominated foreign exchange settlements in connection with import trade showed a minute rise to 20.6 percent in September from 20.5 percent at end-March 1996, the official said.
